newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bomb explodes in Nigerian city, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes in Nigerian city, no injuries.

text.p: A bomb aimed at a military target rocked the western Nigerian city of Ibadan on Monday but there were no injuries, police said.
"It just damaged a police vehicle but there was no casualty," a police spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone from Ibadan, 100 kms (60 miles) north of Lagos.
It was the third bomb blast in southwestern Nigeria, the hotbed of opposition to the military government, in two weeks.
Last week two bombs went off in Lagos wounding five soldiers going to work in an army bus.
The police spokeswoman said the explosion in Ibadan followed a pattern similar to the recent spate of bomb blasts in the country.
"The vehicle was conveying soldiers to work and the bomb went off as it was passing by the busy Eleyele/Jericho junction," she said.
Nigeria has blamed similar explosions on the opposition umbrella NADECO group and its foreign affiliates. The groups deny any involvement.
Africa's most populous nation has been in turmoil since June 1993 when the army annulled a presidential election to restore democracy.

Moshood Abiola, a wealthy businessman from the southwest, who was deemed to have won the annulled vote, has been in detention since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of the military rulers.
In March Nigeria charged 12 dissidents including exiled Nobel Prize-winning writer Wole Soyinka with treason over the bomb explosions.
The magistrate will decide on Tuesday whether her court is competent to hear the treason case.
